design: docs/integration/plan/20261031_migration_commit_orchestration.md (sections 2-10 are the design; section 11 registers the implementation deviations)
implementation: The seven stages (inspect, intent, drain, capture, maintenance, activate, release) run over one append-only hash-chained journal; every record carries the previous digest, so a rewritten or reordered row is refused (MIGRATION_ORCH_CHAIN_INVALID) instead of being replayed.

Fence gaps closed in this wave: the intent is written atomically (temp file, fsync, rename, directory sync) so a truncated intent never reads as an absent maintenance state (G1); unreadable JSON fails closed instead of being admitted (G2); one operation id can no longer have two owners, and the loser cannot release (G4); a drain timeout now leaves a handle only through abandonMigrationIntent, and fence.release() answers MIGRATION_FENCE_NOT_HELD when no exclusive exists (case 20).

Configuration commit accepts an optional explicit operationId and binds fence, plan and startup gate to it; the gate read side only accepts UUID v4, so a caller-supplied non-v4 id answers MIGRATION_ORCH_OPERATION_ID_UNSUPPORTED and an omitted id is randomUUID().

Activation is evaluated, never granted: criteria C1-C5 are recomputed from the live fence, the verified capture and the gate, any single false criterion yields blocked-activation with an activation-refused record, the gate is never written committed, and the result always carries activationSupported:false, postActivationRollbackSupported:false and stopWriteProvable:false.

Recovery re-derives the stage from the journal and advances forward only; a blocked phase records once and is never rewritten into another phase's verdict, cancellation keeps the fence (cancelled-fence-held), and release requires all four hard preconditions (verified data and ledger capture, drain-completed, a terminal gate, a matching owner).

The writers-inventory observation stays advisory: on Windows writerEnumeration is 'unavailable' and on Linux it is 'linux-procfs...'; both paths keep C4/C5 false, so a slice-1 inventory can never be turned into a stop proof.

preservedFailures: G1/G2/G4 are existing fence gaps that were closed only in this wave, not regressions introduced here: a non-atomic intent write and admitted bad JSON (G1/G2), one operation id with two owners (G4), and a drain timeout whose only safe exit is the new evidence-backed abandonMigrationIntent rather than a direct fence release.
operationId is narrowed to UUID v4 because the configuration-commit gate read side only accepts v4; the dispatching agent approved that narrowing and non-v4 input is refused rather than coerced.

Design case 22 (a Linux write handle is advisory, never a stop proof) is skipped on win32 and the Linux leg was NOT executed in this session: the configured Fedora host failed the SSH handshake, so the Linux side of case 22 stays unverified and is not written as verified.

A corrupt intent.json is deliberately not retractable through the API: abandonment refuses it (MIGRATION_FENCE_INTENT_UNREADABLE / digest mismatch) and a human must read the bytes. Fail-closed is intended, but it means an operator cannot recover through the component alone.

The orchestration is not wired into any product entry (design gap G5 / C9): no product code imports it, no startup path calls it, and there is no activate->committed path. This is component evidence only and is not product migration capability.

The three root-regression failures are environmental: tests/remote-auth.native.mjs times out on its fixture HTTPS request, and tests/remote-command-tasks.native.mjs plus tests/remote-write-tasks.native.mjs answer TASK_RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE after ~25s of subprocess readiness. All three are green when run alone (32/27/0/5), so they are concurrency/readiness flakiness and not slice-5 evidence.

The design document's plan links to the two HANDOFF files had to be rewritten as inline code paths (docs/integration/HANDOFF-20261031-KIMI-E77.md, docs/integration/HANDOFF-20261031-GLM.md): a ../HANDOFF-*.md link escapes docs/integration/plan and fails tests/integration-documents.test.mjs. The six-suite figure was restated after review: 60 tests / 59 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip is the composition that swaps rollback readiness for ci-contract (five migration suites plus ci-contract 5), while 61 tests / 60 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip is the five migration suites plus rollback readiness (6); both were measured, both are correct, and the earlier reading that one of them had under-counted by one was wrong.

The intermittent 'fence gate race closes' and 'crashed coordinator' failures were root-caused to a test-side wait race, not a product defect and not introduced by this slice: the fixture (tests/fixtures/migration-fence-holder.mjs) only ever writes 'ACQUIRED' or an error code and never an empty string, but writeFile creates the file before its bytes land and waitFile returned as soon as readFile succeeded, so a readable-but-empty file was mistaken for the fixture's answer. Fixed on the test side only (wait for trimmed non-empty content, still bounded at 15s): tests/migration-fence.native.mjs 5d96ddb2 -> f211feab, tests/migration-fence-hardening.native.mjs d5b9d77e -> b1b763a2, fixture unchanged at 54b27026, and no product byte changed.
